Read `README.md` and current rollout evidence first. Produce exactly one multi-wake target-policy candidate in `solver/`. Keep candidate-specific reasoning in `logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md`, and add or materially revise at least one evidence-backed reusable lesson in `guidance/control_experience.md` from the assigned parent, sampled solver results, and inherited logs. If no positive lesson survives the evidence, record a concrete negative result and what later workers should avoid or test. The candidate is incomplete until both files are updated. Work only inside this Phase 2 workspace.

Use the fish-control bookshelf through this structured transfer protocol:

1. Before the first architecture proposal from the common naive seed, consult `guidance/skills/fish-control-primitives/SKILL.md` and its references.
2. On later iterations, consult it again when the inherited guidance indicates three consecutive completed iterations with neither a new controller mechanism nor a semantic improvement such as a new success, a better termination class, or a meaningfully different useful trajectory.
3. Consultation is required at those moments; adopting a primitive is optional. Do not use the shelf to justify scalar-only gain tuning.
4. If a source informs the edit, record a concise block in `logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md`:

```text
bookshelf_consulted: true
source_domain:
source_mechanism:
transferable_invariant:
nontransferable_details:
policy_translation:
falsification:
```

Translate only the invariant into normalized body-frame observations and the two-joint state-feedback contract. Prefer one mechanism or one small compatible combination. Published gains, species-specific kinematics, exact vortex phases, and task-specific routes are not transferable answers.

I’ll first read the workspace instructions, the current rollout artifacts, and both policy-specific skill protocols. Then I’ll make one candidate only, document its evidence chain, and verify the required files and policy contract.

The bookshelf protocol applies here, and the visual-first protocol requires comparing the best finite rollout with the most informative failure before editing. I’m now anchoring the keyframes to scores, trajectories, force diagnostics, and inherited guidance; the candidate file will remain untouched until that diagnosis is written.

The rollout set has no semantic failure: all four capture under verified direct-uniform still water. Three are byte-identical repetitions of the current mean-preserving demodulator; the fourth is the one-line raw-joint demodulation control. I’m using that weaker captured control as the only informative comparator and will avoid inventing a nonexistent failure case.

The visuals show nearly identical self-propelled arcs: a coherent alternating mid-plane street and tail-connected 3D structures persist through capture, with no advection or instability signature. The remaining measurable weakness is actuator intensity, not route topology. I’m consulting the shelf’s source notes now because the prospective edit uses its “preserve the rhythmic carrier and put correction in a separate bounded channel” invariant.

The proposed single mechanism is an actuator-compatible tangent projection: when a joint is already exactly at the ±260°/T speed boundary, remove only acceleration that points farther outside the feasible set; preserve all reversal commands and all route/carrier computations. On the completed incumbent trace, such unrealizable outward commands occur in 23.45% of logged steps, so this tests a real redundancy while leaving the proven capture architecture intact. I’m recording that hypothesis before touching the candidate, as required.

The candidate now changes only the returned acceleration at an already-active speed boundary; the evaluated route, yaw demodulation, carrier, steering, and all gains are untouched. I’m distilling the reusable evidence boundary into guidance next—especially that this does not license earlier carrier attenuation.

The implementation and both required provenance files are present. Per the workspace contract, I’m now invoking the dedicated non-CFD check runner to validate guidance semantics, the Julia policy interface/schema, and the editable-file boundary.

The configured check-runner model is unavailable in this environment, so the delegated invocation could not start. I’m applying the same `.codex/agents/check-runner.toml` checks directly, as three separate non-CFD commands, and will repair anything they flag.

The first check found a rendered-workspace metadata defect: `README.md` lists the same assigned parent twice with the “copied to guidance” marker, so the checker cannot identify one parent. I’m removing only that duplicate reference entry, then rerunning the required guidance comparison.

The Julia contract check itself is blocked because `julia` is not installed on this runner; the shell also emitted unrelated missing SSH-bootstrap files before reporting `command not found`. I’ll still run the boundary check and add equivalent static schema plus edge-case checks for the new speed projection so the handoff is as complete as this environment permits.

All available checks now pass: guidance semantics, parameter-schema completeness, editable solver boundary, non-empty required files, and a fixed-trace feasibility check showing 709/3024 commands are projected with zero change to the next clamped joint speed. Only the Julia execution check remains unavailable because this image has no Julia binary; I’m doing a final scope and diff audit now.

Implemented exactly one candidate: a speed-envelope tangent projection that removes only infeasible outward acceleration at the active ±260°/T joint-speed limit while preserving the proven capture controller.

Updated:
